signals.name: Micron / AI-memory & chips
signals.label: Burry shorts chips; retail piles in
signals.detail: Burry shorted MU/NVDA/AMAT; MU #1 on WSB
signals.takeaway: The most two-sided consensus name in the market. Michael Burry (now disclosing via Substack after deregistering) revealed fresh shorts on NVIDIA, Applied Materials and the semis ETF on 30 June and shorted Micron directly on 2 July, arguing chips are 'historically extreme' and due a ~30% correction. Yet MU is the #1 most-mentioned WSB ticker (742 mentions) and a congressional favorite, and a 7 July semis rout (weak Samsung, DeepSeek efficiency fears) sank the Nasdaq -1.16%. Consensus-crowded and now openly contested by smart money.

signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Deficit thesis vs rate scars
signals.detail: Silver back <$60 (~$60.4); down ~4% on the week
signals.takeaway: Silver gave back the prior week's ~6% bounce, slipping under $60 to ~$60.4/oz and ending the week down ~4% as firmer oil and renewed US-Iran tension revived higher-for-longer rate bets (10Y ~4.57%, firm dollar). The structural bull case is intact (Silver Institute pegs a widening 46.3Moz 2026 deficit; J.P. Morgan models ~$81 average), but the metal is still ~50% below January's ~$120 peak after June's crash, and the low remains unconfirmed. The single most important line item for this book and its highest-beta risk into the 14 July CPI, which is now the binary that decides the next leg.

signals.name: MP Materials / rare earths
signals.label: Critical-minerals flashpoint
signals.takeaway: China's MOFCOM enforcement mechanism (rewarding tips on unlicensed rare-earth exports and transshipment) went live 1 July, tightening a regime that in June blacklisted MP Materials and USA Rare Earth. China controls ~70% of mining and ~90% of processing/magnets, so each escalation raises the strategic value of Western names (MP — DoD a stakeholder — Lynas, Neo, Energy Fuels) even as the VanEck REMX basket consolidates ~21% off its high. A policy-driven, multi-name theme with a US-government financing floor underneath.

signals.name: SPDR Gold Shares
signals.label: Consolidation with a CB floor
signals.takeaway: Gold is consolidating around $4,000-4,175 after June's ~11% slide. Goldman trimmed its year-end target to ~$4,900 on the view the Fed won't cut in 2026 and fading ETF inflows, while J.P. Morgan stays bullish (~$6,000 by Q4) and the PBoC reportedly ramped official buying to ~8 tonnes in April. A hawkish Fed caps the non-yielding hedge near-term, but central-bank demand and the 14 July CPI are the swings.

signals.name: Inflation / Fed
signals.label: Hawkish hold; CPI is the binary
signals.detail: June minutes done; July hold ~75%; June CPI 14 Jul
signals.takeaway: The June FOMC minutes (Chair Warsh's first meeting, held 3.50-3.75% with a hawkish dot plot — 9 of 19 see a 2026 hike) confirmed a 'some officials saw a case for further hikes' higher-for-longer stance. Attention now pivots to the 14 July June CPI: the oil plunge earlier in June may flip headline slightly negative (~-0.1% m/m, ~3.9% y/y), but core is seen sticky at +0.3% (~2.9% y/y). CME FedWatch prices ~75% odds of a 28-29 July hold and ~25% for a hike, with the 10Y backed up to ~4.57%. Breakevens are squeezed between sticky core and a deflated energy tail.

signals.name: Tencent
signals.label: Buyback + HK tech rip
signals.detail: 1.1m shares / HK$500.7M on 9 Jul; HSTECH +5% on 8 Jul
signals.takeaway: One of Hong Kong's largest repurchase programs — Tencent kept buying back shares almost every session into July (1.1M / HK$500.7M on 9 July, a lighter HK$12.7M tranche 8 July) under the ~912M-share (10%) mandate approved 13 May. The corporate bid coincided with a broad HK tech rip on 8 July (Hang Seng +3%, Hang Seng Tech +5%, Alibaba +12%, Xiaomi +9%, SMIC +7.5%) as post-IPO lock-up fears eased and the domestic-AI bid returned. A near-mechanical conviction signal alongside its AI/gaming/fintech franchises; Xiaomi (HK$20bn), Kuaishou (HK$16bn) and others run parallel HK buybacks.

signals.name: Microsoft / Mag-7
signals.label: Tri-constituency consensus
signals.detail: Held by super-investors, Congress & retail alike
signals.takeaway: Microsoft, Nvidia and Meta are the tightest overlap across all three tracked constituencies — super-investor 13Fs (MSFT is the #2 Dataroma holding), Congress (Gottheimer bought MSFT calls; ~166 congressional buys) and retail/WSB. A vivid split remains under the surface: Pershing opened a ~$2.1B MSFT stake in the same window the Gates Foundation Trust sold its last shares, and Burry is shorting the adjacent chip complex. Consensus-long but increasingly contested at the mega-cap-tech top.

signals.name: Energy Select Sector
signals.label: Congress vs. crude
signals.detail: Members keep buying energy as WTI sits ~$70
signals.takeaway: Republican members (Hern's Coterra+Devon, Foxx's ARLP coal MLP) keep accumulating traditional energy on the power-demand thesis even as crude sits near 4-month lows — WTI ~$70.5 and Brent ~$72-73 after OPEC+ added another 188kbpd and Gulf exports normalized. A tug-of-war between structural AI-power demand and a fully-deflated geopolitical premium.

congress.rationale: The West Virginia Republican sold Citigroup stock (transaction 16 June, disclosed 6 July 2026), trimming a large-bank holding.
congress.deepDive: Capito, a senior Republican senator, disclosed the Citigroup disposal in early July, one of the freshest Senate filings in the window. The sale of a money-center bank comes as the yield curve normalized and big-bank Q2 earnings approach mid-July, so it reads as routine rebalancing or profit-taking rather than a sector call. As a member subject to STOCK Act reporting, even modest bank trades draw scrutiny given committee overlaps.

congress.rationale: The Michigan Democrat bought AT&T stock (transaction 29 June, disclosed 2 July 2026), a defensive, high-yield telecom.
congress.deepDive: Peters added AT&T, a dividend-paying telecom that fits a defensive, income-oriented tilt amid a hawkish Fed and higher-for-longer rates. The purchase is a low-beta holding that can cushion a portfolio if rate-driven multiple compression hits growth names. As a senior senator, his relatively infrequent single-name buys draw modest STOCK Act attention.

congress.rationale: The Louisiana Democrat's newly filed financial disclosure (18 June 2026) revealed a very large NVIDIA position, the single biggest line in an AI-heavy portfolio.
congress.deepDive: Fields, a freshman member, disclosed a concentrated mega-cap tech book led by a seven-figure NVIDIA stake alongside Microsoft and Apple (each up to $500K). The scale of the NVIDIA line — up to $5M — is unusually large for a House member and lands amid an intense AI/semis tape now openly shorted by Burry. As an annual-disclosure surfacing rather than a fresh periodic transaction, it reflects accumulated positioning, but the size makes it conspicuous for copy-traders and STOCK Act watchers alike.

congress.rationale: One of Congress's most active traders, the California Democrat trimmed GoDaddy (transaction 16 June, disclosed 3 July 2026) while adding industrials.
congress.deepDive: Cisneros is among the House's highest-volume traders, and the GoDaddy sale paired with an Enerpac Tool Group (EPAC) buy reads as a rotation from web-services software toward industrials. His frequent two-sided trading through managed accounts mutes the direct signal, but the aggregate direction favors cyclicals over software — echoing a broader institutional tilt. STOCK Act scrutiny applies given his committee assignments.

congress.rationale: The Pennsylvania Republican sold NVIDIA and bought SpaceX private shares (disclosed 3 July 2026), rotating from public AI beta into private space-tech.
congress.deepDive: Meuser's paired NVIDIA sale and SpaceX (SPCX) purchase is a notable rotation from a richly valued, now-shorted public AI leader into illiquid private space-tech exposure. Trimming NVIDIA near highs while chasing a marquee private name reflects a barbell of de-risking public tech and reaching for asymmetric private upside. Amount ranges on the aggregation feed were not fully specified; the direction is the signal.

congress.rationale: The prolific New Jersey Democrat and ex-Microsoft executive bought large Microsoft call options plus semiconductor and cybersecurity names (Analog Devices, Palo Alto Networks).
congress.deepDive: Gottheimer is one of the most active traders in the House, and a six-to-seven-figure notional Microsoft call position is a leveraged bullish bet on AI monetization through Copilot and Azure. Pairing MSFT with Palo Alto Networks and Analog Devices deepens a semiconductor-and-security tilt aligned with the AI buildout. Because the trades run through Morgan Stanley managed accounts the direct signal is muted, but the aggregate direction is a clear growth/AI-infrastructure lean.

congress.rationale: The Ohio Republican bought Installed Building Products alongside Chevron (disclosed 2 July 2026), a housing/construction and energy pairing.
congress.deepDive: Taylor's purchase of Installed Building Products is a bet on US housing/construction resilience, and pairing it with Chevron adds traditional-energy exposure in the same filing. The housing pick aligns with the week's fund-flow rotation into rate-sensitive real-economy cyclicals, while the Chevron add fits the Republican pattern of accumulating energy on the power-demand thesis. Dollar range approximate on the aggregation feed.

congress.rationale: The Arizona Democrat exited Trulieve Cannabis (disclosed 29 June 2026), removing a speculative cannabis position.
congress.deepDive: Stanton's disposal of Trulieve Cannabis removes a high-beta, regulation-sensitive holding whose fortunes hinge on stalled federal cannabis reform. The exit reads as de-risking a speculative small-cap rather than a broad sector call. As a member subject to STOCK Act reporting, even niche disposals are logged, though the signaling value here is modest.

congress.rationale: Disclosed 23 June, the former Speaker (via her husband) bought 200 Uber call options (~$50 strike, March 2027 expiry), a leveraged bullish bet on the rideshare/autonomy platform.
congress.deepDive: Pairing Uber with Intel calls in the same late-May filing extends Pelosi's preference for long-dated calls on large, liquid franchises with secular tailwinds — here the AV/robotaxi optionality and improving free-cash-flow profile that have made Uber a hedge-fund favorite (Ackman's Pershing Square holds it). The March 2027 expiry gives the thesis ample runway, and the size and leverage make it a clear directional call. Pelosi's options trades draw intense STOCK Act scrutiny and retail copy-trading.

congress.rationale: The former Speaker bought 200 Intel call options (~$50 strike, March 2027 expiry) — her first trades since January 2026 and a large, leveraged bullish bet on the US semiconductor champion.
congress.deepDive: A seven-figure notional Intel call position is a conspicuous, high-conviction wager on a turnaround at the embattled chipmaker as US re-shoring, CHIPS-Act fab subsidies and AI demand converge. Buying deep-dated calls (March 2027) maximizes leverage and time for the thesis, consistent with her pattern of long-dated call buying on mega-cap tech. As a senior member with deep visibility into tech and trade policy, even routine Pelosi disclosures draw STOCK Act scrutiny and heavy copy-trading.

congress.rationale: A sizable sale of NVIDIA, locking in gains from a richly valued position — notable from a senator who publicly criticizes congressional stock trading.
congress.deepDive: Whitehouse has long advocated ethics reform and supports restricting member trading, making his own six-figure NVIDIA sale politically conspicuous. The trade, paired with an Oracle sale, points to de-risking from high-multiple AI infrastructure names after a strong run — prescient given Burry's subsequent chip shorts and the 7 July semis rout. The $100K-$250K size is large relative to typical House disclosures and amplifies the optics.

congress.rationale: The Oklahoma Republican added Coterra Energy alongside Devon Energy, a concentrated bullish bet on domestic oil-and-gas producers.
congress.deepDive: Hern, a wealthy McDonald's franchisee turned congressman, frequently trades energy names that mirror Oklahoma's hydrocarbon-heavy economy. The paired Coterra and Devon buys double down on upstream E&P even as crude sits near 4-month lows, reading as a structural power-demand/value bet rather than a spot-price call. As a senior Ways and Means member, his energy positions intersect with tax and energy policy he helps write.

congress.rationale: The North Carolina Republican bought Alliance Resource Partners, a coal producer and high-yield MLP, aligning with a pro-fossil-fuel income tilt.
congress.deepDive: Alliance Resource Partners is one of the largest US coal producers and pays a high distribution yield, a popular income play among energy-friendly Republican members. The coal bet fits a 2026 theme of traditional-energy accumulation tied to rising electricity demand from data centers and electrification. As an MLP, ARLP carries distinctive pass-through tax characteristics relevant to disclosure.

congress.rationale: The Florida Democrat added Gilead Sciences, a defensive large-cap biotech, within a broader AI/defense-leaning portfolio (AVGO, NVDA, ADI).
congress.deepDive: The Gilead buy adds a steady, dividend-paying biotech to a book otherwise tilted toward AI-infrastructure beneficiaries, a lower-beta holding that can cushion a growth-heavy portfolio if rate-driven multiple compression hits high-flyers. Pairing it with a sale of drug-distributor Cencora the same day reads as a rotation within healthcare rather than a sector call. His frequent two-sided trading draws routine STOCK Act scrutiny.

congress.rationale: A companion to his NVIDIA sale (disclosed 3 July 2026): the Pennsylvania Republican bought SpaceX private shares, adding illiquid space-tech exposure.
congress.deepDive: Buying SpaceX private shares while selling NVIDIA rotates from a shorted, richly valued public AI leader into a marquee private name — SpaceX also joined the Nasdaq-100 proxy conversation as SPCX exposure broadened in July. The move reflects reaching for asymmetric private upside at the expense of crowded public tech beta. Amount range approximate on the aggregation feed.

superInvestors.name: Scion Asset Management
superInvestors.rationale: Michael Burry disclosed a direct short on Micron on 2 July 2026 (entry ~$1,051.87), on top of fresh 30 June shorts against NVIDIA, Applied Materials and the iShares Semiconductor ETF, arguing AI chips face a ~30% correction.
superInvestors.deepDive: Having deregistered as an SEC adviser in late 2025, Burry no longer files 13Fs and now discloses via Substack — so these are his freshest, most public bets. He calls Micron 'cyclical like no other' (34 drawdowns >30% over 42 years, ~4% median ROIC) and says it is more extended above its 200-day average than at any time since 1984. The thesis lands just as a 7 July semiconductor rout (weak Samsung, DeepSeek efficiency fears) validated the caution. This is the single most notable new smart-money move of the window and a direct counter to the consensus AI-hardware long.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
superInvestors.rationale: Berkshire's Alphabet stake has grown to roughly $41B — now larger than its Coca-Cola position — and on 1 July Buffett said the 2026 pullback 'wasn't big enough' to deploy the record ~$397B cash pile.
superInvestors.deepDive: The Alphabet position, aggressively built in Q1 and appreciating since, has become one of Berkshire's largest bets and an unusual mega-cap-growth lean for a value house, premised on Alphabet's Gemini/Cloud AI leadership and search cash flows. Buffett's comment that the dip was too shallow to move the cash mountain underscores a defensive, capital-preservation posture in the Abel transition. Late June also saw Berkshire top up the Japanese trading houses (Mitsui ~10.83%, Marubeni ~10.32%), extending its highest-conviction non-US theme.

superInvestors.name: Trump Media & Technology (DJT)
superInvestors.rationale: Trump Media disclosed buying ~$2B of bitcoin and related securities — roughly two-thirds of its ~$3B in assets — pivoting toward a crypto-treasury strategy; the stock rose on the news.
superInvestors.deepDive: The bitcoin pivot converts a large slug of DJT's balance sheet into a levered crypto proxy, sensitive to the same rate backdrop weighing on BTC (~$64K, a 21-month-low bounce). Separately, the proposed US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve stalled on 6 July amid a Treasury-Commerce turf war over ~328k seized BTC (~$25B), now mediated by the DOJ's Office of Legal Counsel — a policy overhang for the whole digital-asset complex. A high-visibility, politically charged crypto bet rather than a diversified allocation.

superInvestors.name: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Trust
superInvestors.rationale: Buffett delayed his annual Berkshire-stock gift for the first time in ~20 years (disclosed 29-30 June) pending a review of the foundation's Jeffrey Epstein ties; the Trust's ~$33B equity book is now ~43% in two names, led by Berkshire, after selling its last Microsoft.
superInvestors.deepDive: The pause on Buffett's roughly annual multibillion-dollar donation — possibly resolved in his Thanksgiving letter — is a rare, headline-grabbing break in a decades-long relationship and injects uncertainty into the foundation's funding cadence. With Microsoft fully exited in Q1, Berkshire and Waste Management now anchor a highly concentrated portfolio. The concentration removes single-stock diversification but leaves the Trust heavily exposed to Berkshire's own defensive, cash-heavy posture.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
superInvestors.rationale: Berkshire fully exited Visa (~$2.91B) and Mastercard in Q1, a sharp reversal on the payment-network duopoly, part of a broad sell-down alongside UnitedHealth and Amazon exits.
superInvestors.deepDive: Dumping both Visa and Mastercard (~$5B combined) marks a clean break from payments after years of ownership, coinciding with Berkshire remaining a net seller and trimming its holding count. With a ~$397B cash pile, the moves reinforce a defensive, capital-preservation posture in the Abel transition. The rotation out of payments and into Alphabet/Delta reflects a meaningful reshuffling of sector exposure.

superInvestors.name: Pershing Square
superInvestors.rationale: Ackman's Pershing Square initiated a ~$2.1B Microsoft position (~15% of the ~$13.7B portfolio), a significant new mega-cap tech bet for a famously concentrated ~10-stock book.
superInvestors.deepDive: The Microsoft buy signals conviction in AI monetization through Copilot and Azure as a durable compounder and instantly became a top holding alongside Brookfield, Amazon and Uber. Notably, Ackman added Microsoft just as the Gates Foundation Trust was selling its last shares — a vivid illustration of opposing institutional views. No fresh Pershing move surfaced this window; the latest concrete news remains the May stake.

superInvestors.name: Duquesne Family Office
superInvestors.rationale: Druckenmiller opened a new ~195,955-share Broadcom position (~$60.65M) while exiting Alphabet and nearly eliminating Amazon, concentrating his AI bet on the picks-and-shovels layer.
superInvestors.deepDive: Buying Broadcom while dumping mega-cap platforms shows Druckenmiller favoring the custom-silicon/networking infrastructure that directly benefits from hyperscaler AI capex. Natera became his single largest holding (~18% of the ~$3.4B book), and new biotech buys (Caris, Revolution Medicines) round out a healthcare-innovation theme. The high-turnover profile is intact; 13F assets fell ~22% QoQ.

superInvestors.name: Bridgewater Associates
superInvestors.rationale: Bridgewater boosted NVIDIA, Broadcom and Micron and opened Taiwan Semiconductor while exiting enterprise-software names (Salesforce, ServiceNow, Workday, Adobe) — a clean chips-over-software rotation.
superInvestors.deepDive: For a systematic macro shop, leaning into a full-stack semiconductor bet — foundry (TSM), GPUs (NVDA), networking (AVGO), memory (MU) — reflects models favoring the AI-capex theme over SaaS margins. The firm's flagship Pure Alpha fund gained ~8.1% in H1 2026 (its AI-driven AIA fund also +8.1%) under CEO Nir Bar Dea, ~$102B AUM. The rotation positions Bridgewater to benefit if AI-infrastructure spending keeps outrunning software re-acceleration.

superInvestors.name: Appaloosa
superInvestors.rationale: David Tepper boosted Whirlpool by nearly 2,000% q/q to a ~$432.3M position (~5.85% of the portfolio), a deep-cyclical contrarian bet, while adding to Amazon (top holding at ~15%).
superInvestors.deepDive: The massive Whirlpool add is Appaloosa's most aggressive single move of the quarter, a contrarian wager on a housing/consumer-durables recovery and a depressed valuation. Nearly doubling Amazon diverges sharply from Druckenmiller's near-exit, again highlighting split views among top investors. No clearly fresh late-June/July Appaloosa move surfaced; reports of China/NVDA shifts trace to older 2024 and Q1 data.

superInvestors.name: Soros Fund Management
superInvestors.rationale: Soros increased NVIDIA alongside Taiwan Semiconductor and Electronic Arts adds and new CoreWeave (CRWV) puts, within a ~$7.36B, 263-position book led by Amazon, EA, NVDA, TSM and Alphabet.
superInvestors.deepDive: The NVIDIA add signals continued conviction in the AI-compute leader, while the CRWV puts and TSM options overlays are classic Soros macro-hedge expressions — asymmetric protection rather than an outright directional call. Trimming AMZN/GOOGL/MSFT/CRM suggests rotation within mega-cap tech rather than broad risk-off. No fresh 13F this window; Q2 filings are due 14 August.

superInvestors.name: Tiger Global
superInvestors.rationale: Tiger Global lifted Taiwan Semiconductor ~49% to a top-4 holding (~8% of the ~$22.85B portfolio), complementing large NVIDIA and Broadcom positions and new MercadoLibre and Netflix buys.
superInvestors.deepDive: The TSM add deepens Tiger's AI-infrastructure exposure at the foundry level, aligning with parallel moves by Bridgewater and Soros into TSM the same quarter — a clear cross-fund chip consensus. Within a book anchored by Alphabet and NVIDIA, it reinforces a concentrated bet on the AI-compute supply chain. Tiger and Burry both bought MELI in Q1, a rare growth-plus-deep-value convergence.

superInvestors.name: Scion Asset Management
superInvestors.rationale: Burry fully liquidated his Chinese technology basket (Alibaba, JD.com, Baidu) in Q1 2026, reversing prior bullishness and rotating into beaten-down Western large caps (MELI, LULU, ADBE, PYPL).
superInvestors.deepDive: The complete China exit mirrored David Tepper trimming Alibaba in the same period, suggesting shared caution on Chinese equities amid policy and geopolitical risk. Rotating proceeds into MercadoLibre and Lululemon at multi-year lows is vintage Burry deep-value contrarianism. Notably the long-only 13F showed no puts — but Burry's subsequent 2026 chip shorts confirm his filings historically understate his options book.

insiders.rationale: Tencent repurchased ~1.1M shares for HK$500.7 million on 9 July 2026 (with a lighter 27,600-share / HK$12.7M tranche on 8 July), the latest in a near-daily buyback streak running ~HK$500M tranches on 2, 3 and 9 July under the ~912M-share (10%) mandate approved at the 13 May 2026 AGM.
insiders.deepDive: Company buybacks are a strong corporate-level conviction signal, and Tencent runs one of the largest repurchase programs in Hong Kong. The relentless daily cadence into July reflects a commitment to shrinking the share count and offsetting dilution from share-based compensation, with the read-through bullish for holders as the stock trades ~HK$450-470; the buyback bid coincided with a broad HK-tech rally on 8 July (Hang Seng Tech +5%). Tencent is not alone — Xiaomi (a HK$20bn program), Kuaishou (HK$16bn) and Li Auto are all running parallel HK repurchases. Unlike a director's open-market buy, an issuer repurchase signals management's capital-allocation confidence rather than a single insider's personal bet.

insiders.role: EVP & Chief Sustainability and Development Officer
insiders.rationale: Newmont's EVP sold 3,000 shares (~$277K) at $92.38 on 1 July 2026 (filed 6 July) under a Rule 10b5-1 plan dated 17 December 2025, leaving 43,315 shares — routine, pre-scheduled selling at the world's largest gold miner (a top GDX holding).
insiders.deepDive: This is a scheduled 10b5-1 disposal rather than a discretionary conviction sell, so the signal is muted — executives routinely diversify into strength, and gold near $4,150 makes profit-taking unremarkable. As the largest US-filing gold producer and a core GDX constituent, Newmont insider activity is a useful read on miner sentiment, and the absence of any open-market buying alongside these sales is consistent with a sector that already re-rated hard before June's pullback. Most large GDX/SILJ miners are Canadian foreign private issuers reporting on SEDI rather than US Form 4, so Newmont is one of the few that surfaces in SEC filings.

insiders.rationale: Hecla Mining's General Counsel had ~23,973 shares withheld for tax on RSUs that vested 22 June 2026, with the CFO seeing similar RSU vesting/withholding — equity-compensation events, not open-market buying or selling, at a core silver miner (SILJ/GDX).
insiders.deepDive: These are routine compensation/tax-withholding transactions rather than directional trades, so the signal value is low, but they are among the few recent US Form 4 filings in the largely-Canadian silver-miner universe. Hecla is the largest US primary silver producer and a SILJ constituent, making its filings a window into silver-complex insider behavior that SEDI-reporting peers otherwise hide. No open-market buying accompanied the vesting, consistent with insiders neither chasing nor fading the post-crash silver bounce.

insiders.rationale: Coeur Mining's EVP Exploration made a small open-market purchase of 635 shares (~$10.8K) at $16.95 on 12 June 2026 — the most recent verified Coeur insider transaction, a modest genuine-conviction buy at a US-domiciled silver/gold producer (latest available).
insiders.deepDive: Coeur is one of the few US-domiciled precious-metals miners that files Form 4, making it a window into silver-complex insider sentiment that the largely-Canadian SILJ/SLVP universe hides on SEDI. A small EVP open-market purchase is a modest genuine-conviction buy against a backdrop of plan-based executive selling elsewhere in the sector. With silver whipsawing in the high-$50s to low-$60s, the lack of sizable open-market buying suggests insiders see fair-to-full value rather than a fresh entry point after the multi-quarter run. No newer Coeur Form 4 has surfaced in the past two weeks, so this remains the latest available.

insiders.rationale: DBS CEO Tan Su Shan sold 100,000 shares at S$60.12 on 15 May 2026, leaving ~1.3 million shares (0.048% of the bank), a partial profit-taking trim shortly after the stock first pushed above S$60 — the most recent verified insider move on the SGX-listed holdings (latest available).
insiders.deepDive: The sale came days after DBS reported 1Q2026 net profit of S$2.93 billion (up 1% y/y, 24% q/q) and as the stock hit record territory; DBS has since pushed to a fresh ~S$67 all-time high into its 6 August results. As Singapore's largest lender's first female CEO, Tan retains a sizeable 1.3 million-share holding, so this is a liquidity/diversification trim rather than a loss of confidence. CEO sells into all-time highs are common and often tax-driven, but can cap near-term sentiment given DBS's elevated ~2.2x book valuation and NIM sensitivity to falling SORA. No within-window (24 June-8 July) substantial-shareholder or director-interest change was verifiable for the SGX holdings this run; DBS continues a S$3bn buyback through 2027.
